evidence.excerpt: Standard readability formulas derived from English are poorly suited to morphologically rich languages where syllable counts and sentence boundaries behave differently. This paper reports the systematic adaptation of a Flesch–Kincaid-style index for Serbian, drawing on a corpus of 180 patient information leaflets collected from pharmacies and outpatient clinics in Vojvodina between 2008 and 2010. The corpus was manually segmented and syllabified, and comprehension was tested with 96 participants using a validated cloze procedure. Regression analysis identified an optimal formula weighting average syllables per word (β = 0.61) and average words per sentence (β = 0.29) against cloze scores (R² = 0.74). The resulting Serbian Readability Index (SRI) is compared with a naive transliteration of the original Flesch–Kincaid formula; the SRI shows significantly better predictive validity (F-change p < .001). Normative data for six text-type categories are provided, along with a scoring spreadsheet distributed as supplementary material.
